Name: lensing_kinematic_imf_tomography_jwster1
Title: Resolving the Dark Matter–IMF Degeneracy in Massive Quiescent Galaxies at z~2 with Spatially Resolved Lensing, Stellar Kinematics, and Spectro-Photometric IMF Tomography
Experiment: We will carry out a joint strong-lensing, stellar-kinematic, and stellar-population study of the JWST-ER1 system, which hosts a complete Einstein ring around a massive compact quiescent lens at z~2. Datasets: (1) existing JWST NIRCam COSMOS-Web imaging in multiple bands for lens and source reconstruction; (2) new JWST NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy covering 1.7-3.1 um at R~2700 to secure lens and source redshifts, map spatially resolved stellar kinematics, and measure IMF-sensitive absorption features including the Ca II triplet, Na I 8200 doublet, and FeH Wing-Ford band; (3) ancillary optical/near-IR photometry from COSMOS for SED priors. Metrics: Bayesian evidence, dark matter fraction within the Einstein radius f_DM(<theta_E)=1-M_*/M_lens, IMF mismatch parameter alpha=M_*(lensing+dynamics)/M_*(Chabrier SED), radial gradients in stellar mass-to-light ratio, reduced chi-square of the lens reconstruction, and posterior uncertainties on the radial mass profile. Baseline comparisons: (i) standard Chabrier IMF plus NFW dark matter, (ii) Salpeter/bottom-heavy IMF plus NFW, (iii) free constant IMF normalization plus NFW, (iv) radially varying IMF plus contracted NFW, (v) parametric Sersic lens model versus free-form lens potential. Expected outcomes: The combined data will show whether the mass discrepancy is resolved by a globally bottom-heavy IMF, by a spatially varying stellar mass-to-light ratio, or by a substantial dark matter component. If the dark matter fraction remains high within the Einstein radius after flexible IMF recovery, the system would indicate an unexpectedly dense dark matter distribution. Ablations: (a) remove kinematic constraints and re-fit with lensing plus photometry only; (b) remove lensing constraints and use only kinematics plus SED fitting; (c) assume solar abundance rather than alpha-enhanced stellar populations; (d) use photometric instead of spectroscopic redshifts; (e) replace spatially resolved kinematics with a single integrated velocity dispersion; (f) restrict the IMF shape to standard unbroken power laws rather than a flexible low-mass turnover.
